judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-4.2 ('Selects and uses suitable units and tools for measuring different attributes of the objects and evaluates the conservation of attributes like length and volume') within CG-4 on measuring attributes. The Class-3 item and its LC target the invariance concept 'Evaluate the conservation of length'; the Class-4 item and its LC target a procedural measuring skill, 'Measure the capacity of vessels in millilitres using measuring containers'. They address different attributes (length vs. capacity) and different skill kinds (conceptual conservation vs. standard-unit measurement with tools), so the Class-3 item is not shown to be a developmental support for the Class-4 capacity procedure; the rank gap alone, shared parent, page proximity, and stopword-only token overlap ('of', 'the') do not establish dependency. There is, however, substantive same-domain coherence: both operationalise the same competency's attribute-measurement strand (conservation of attributes and use of suitable measuring tools/units), supporting a symmetric relatesTo. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so finer-grained sequencing evidence may exist but is not available here.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Competency C-2.3 (relationships among operations; applying the four operations) within CG-2 (fluency with whole numbers and the four operations). The Class-4 item (rank 3) is 'Visualisation of tables', with LC 'Visualise multiplication tables'; the Class-5 item (rank 4) is division of three- and four-digit numbers by two-digit and single-digit divisors, with LCs for each division case. Fluency with and visualisation of multiplication tables directly supports estimating quotients and executing multi-digit division, so proficiency in the lower-rank Class-4 content plausibly supports success in the higher-rank Class-5 content; direction is lower-to-higher (second_to_first). This is a substantive operational extension, not mere wording overlap (the token/trigram overlap evidence is trivial). judgment.rationale: Both are Class-1 Content statements (rank 0, identical coordinate) under the same Competency C-1.3 'Groups objects using two or more attributes or properties'. The first classifies concrete objects (leaves, seeds, beads, pebbles, buttons) by colour, size and similar shape; the second classifies objects by observable attributes such as flat and round, with its LC referencing flat and round/curved surfaces. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 (rank 4) Content bullets under C-3.1/CG-3 on angles, so direction rests on substantive content, not rank. The second SFI ('Identify angles in things around us using turns', LC: identify angles in things around us using turns) establishes the basic angle concept as a turn and its recognition in everyday objects; the first SFI ('Understands importance of 90 degrees, recognises angles as smaller or bigger than 90', LCs: understand the importance of 90 degrees; recognise angles as smaller or bigger than 90 degrees) extends that recognition into quantified comparison against the right angle as a benchmark. Proficiency in identifying/perceiving angles as turns supports success in judging angles relative to 90 degrees, so this is substantive extension rather than generic repetition; the shared 'angles' token alone was not treated as sufficient. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and same-rank ordering is inferred from content semantics only.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs on calendar-based time. The Class-2 item '• Months of the year' (C-1.10, describing duration with familiar units of time; LCs 'Name the months of the year in sequence' and 'Describe the duration of events using months as a unit of time') establishes the year's month structure and month-as-unit reasoning. The Class-3 item '• Number of days in a year' (C-4.4, estimating time; LC 'State the number of days in a year') requires aggregating the calendar year, which in this framework's Class-3 row sits alongside days-in-each-month. Knowing the months that compose a year and their use as time units supports success in quantifying the total days in a year, so the lower-ranked Class-2 (rank 1) item builds towards the Class-3 (rank 2) item; this is substantive extension from naming/sequencing months to numerically quantifying the year, not generic repetition. Endpoint ancestors (CG/Competency) lack developmental coordinates and are context only; both endpoints' source evidence is truncated, but the retained bullet text, LCs, and resolved Class coordinates are sufficient.
